artboards.title: C — One course at a time

annotations.text:
Student page — mastery in the context of each course.

Today the page says "Mastered — 10 lessons", which hides that those 10 are all one course and that the course has 25. Real numbers from the local DB: Perseverence 25 published lessons, Belonie 38, Mount Fleuri 36, Pointe Larue 25.

A — Course accordion. Every course is a row carrying its own fraction; the one with live work is open, the rest collapse to a line. Scales to any number of courses and puts the denominator where it belongs.
Tradeoff: a lesson is always one click away, and a student working across three courses has three things to expand.

B — Summary strip + one table. The fractions are cards at the top; clicking one filters the single lesson table below. Nothing is hidden behind a disclosure, and the cards read at a glance.
Tradeoff: two regions to keep in sync, and the card strip wraps to a second row once a student has more than four courses.

C — One course at a time. The tab bar becomes the course list, each tab carrying its fraction, and the panel below is that course banded Open / Mastered / Not started — the shape the page already has, scoped to one course.
Tradeoff: you cannot see two courses at once, and the tab bar gets crowded past five courses.

Edge case all three must handle: two of this student's courses (Geography S3, Mathematics S3) have 0 published lessons, so the honest fraction is 0/0. Worth deciding whether those courses appear at all.
